content.text:
Green. Here's how I addressed the two findings.

**Finding 1 — hand-rolled JSON serialization. Agreed and fixed.**
Removed `OwnerCreatedEvent.toJson()` and the entire `quote(...)` escape table. The record now carries `@JsonPropertyOrder({"seq","ownerId","customerCode","membershipLevel","event"})`, with the constant `event` exposed as a `@JsonProperty("event")` accessor. `AuditOwnerCreated` takes the project's Jackson `ObjectMapper` as an injected parameter (OfficeFloor resolves it as a Spring bean, the same `tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper` the DTOs use) and calls `objectMapper.writeValueAsString(event)`. Structured audit output now goes through the one serialization path the rest of the app uses; the emitted line is byte-identical to before (`{"seq":1,"ownerId":11,"customerCode":"NSW-16E6609E","membershipLevel":1,"event":"OWNER_CREATED"}`).

Note on imports: databind is `tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper` (Jackson 3), but the annotations remain `com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.*` — matching how the existing `model/*` classes import `@JsonIgnore`.

**Finding 2 — "primary identifier" abstraction only in a comment. Agreed and lifted to the domain.**
Added `Owner.primaryIdentifier()`, which returns the `customerCode` today and is documented as the single place that changes when the code is unified into `memberId`. The audit step now calls `owner.primaryIdentifier()` instead of holding the intent in a local variable + prose, so the "one edit" promise is real at the domain level and any future consumer inherits it. I deliberately named it `primaryIdentifier()` (not a `get*` bean accessor) so it stays a derived domain concept and doesn't become a new MapStruct-mapped / Jackson-serialized property on the entity.

Both the single acceptance test (`coreEventCarriesIdAndIdentifier`) and the full `./mvnw test` build pass. No git repo here, so no commit was made — say the word if you'd like one.
